title: CICFlowMeter CSV is the standard input for IDS classification
notes:
발표 설명
Prior XGB, TabPFN, SOTA, and proposed-model experiments used CICFlowMeter CSV vectors as classification inputs. Many IDS tabular-classification studies also trained and evaluated with the supplied flow statistics. The right half shows how CIC-IDS2017 produced this CSV: network traffic was captured as PCAP, then CICFlowMeter grouped packets into flows and calculated duration, packet-count, IAT, and flag statistics. A CSV row is a summary of these fixed statistics, not the packet sequence itself.

title: Two issues in CSV-based IDS classification
notes:
발표 설명
The CSV-based evaluation revealed two issues. First, some head attacks retained high F1 even after their label budget was reduced sharply, so the representation and task difficulty should be checked before collecting more labels. Second, some rows had identical flow statistics but different labels. This does not mean that every label is wrong; it means that the current statistical representation cannot let a deterministic classifier predict both labels correctly. The next two slides show the observations through performance curves and literal source-CSV rows.

title: Some head attacks already have high F1 with few labels
notes:
발표 설명
This figure extends the earlier CSV-based EXP87 attack-only condition from n = 2 to n = 450. Macro F1 still rises after n = 20, so the entire dataset is not fully saturated. However, head classes such as DDoS and Bot already reach high F1 around n = 20 and change little relative to n = 450. Web attacks remain low even with a larger label budget. Thus, the high average does not mean that every attack is easy: early head saturation and residual tail errors must be examined separately. This is a diagnostic of attack-to-attack classification, not IDS detection with benign traffic included.

title: Identical features, different classes in CIC2018 CSV
notes:
발표 설명
This slide audits the ten original CIC2018 CICFlowMeter CSV files, rather than an NF-v3-derived input. Rows were grouped when all 78 statistical fields common to every file agreed after excluding timestamps and flow identifiers. The table shows literal source-CSV values: displayed fields and the omitted 69 fields are identical, but the NF-v3 class differs. The bars retain the order benign, ddos, bot, dos, bf, inf, web. Their length and endpoint show the share and number of rows from each class in identical-feature, different-class groups. These values do not imply a single cause or that every label is wrong; they show why the representation and label-generation evidence must be examined together.

title: A PCAP-based CIC2018 representation pipeline
notes:
발표 설명
CICFlowMeter calculates CSV features using pre-specified flow rules and statistics. The new pipeline preserves PCAP, time, and label linkage while a packet-sequence encoder generates embeddings and PCA is fit only on the training split. The encoder interface is interchangeable, so netFound, ET-BERT, and NetMamba can be compared with the same inputs, split, and evaluation. Each new vector space is first audited for identical embeddings with different labels and for PCAP label evidence. XGB and TabPFN baselines, few-shot learning curves, and classwise F1 then test whether early head saturation persists in the new representation.

title: Summary
notes:
발표 설명
The presentation has three steps. Existing IDS classifiers used fixed CICFlowMeter statistics from CSV inputs. Inspection of those inputs identified early saturation for some head attacks and identical-feature, different-class rows in the original CSV. The next step is to measure both phenomena again on new CIC2018 vectors created by PCAP encoders, using the same audit and baseline protocol. Only after verifying whether the representation reduces conflicts and improves separation of tail or emerging attacks can a classification benefit from the new representation or model design be assessed.
